subject: SIG packaging: manifest checksum mismatch during Whistic bulk ingest
messages:
From: Elena Bates <elena.bates@acmeinc.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-18 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SIG bundle upload — missing files and checksum mismatch

Hi Tessa,

We tried to ingest the SIG bundle you uploaded to the Whistic portal this morning. The portal returned an error that several files failed checksum validation and the manifest appears to have mismatched hashes (screenshot attached). A couple of files also show as a different file size than listed in the manifest.

Can you confirm:
- Which manifest checksum algorithm you used (MD5 / SHA256)?
- Whether PDFs were exported with OCR layers or as flattened PDF/A?
- If you can repackage and provide a signed manifest with per-file SHA256 checksums, we can retry the bulk ingest.

We need the bundle ingested by end of day Friday to keep the procurement window. Please advise ETA.

Thanks,
Elena Bates
Sr. Procurement Manager
Acme Inc.

Attachments: acme_portal_screenshot.png
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Elena Bates <elena.bates@acmeinc.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-18 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SIG bundle upload — missing files and checksum mismatch

Thanks for the heads up, Elena — sorry for the hassle. I'm pulling the upload logs now and looping in Karthik (portal ingestion) and Marissa (compliance ops).

Quick answers up-front:
- We produced the manifest with SHA256, but it looks like an older export step used CRLF line endings when composing the CSV which can change the computed checksum on some systems.
- PDFs were exported from our SIG packager as PDF/A with searchable OCR layers turned on by default. We can re-export flattened PDFs on request.

Plan: Karthik will regenerate a per-file SHA256 manifest (unix line endings), produce a flattened PDF/A set for the ~6 files that failed, and produce a signed manifest. We will then perform a Whistic bulk upload using the API and share the upload link and logs.

Target ETA: repackage + reupload within 6 hours (EOD target). If that slips we'll get a staged upload for the smallest docs first so you can complete the intake.

Attaching the original manifest we used for reference.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachment: original_manifest.csv
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Elena Bates <elena.bates@acmeinc.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-18 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SIG bundle upload — missing files and checksum mismatch

Hi all,

I dug into the Whistic ingest logs and reproduced the checksum failures locally. Root cause summary:
- The manifest we generated used CRLF (
) line endings when concatenating the CSV on a Windows build agent. The Whistic bulk API and a few of Acme's verification tools compute SHA256 over bytes; different line endings change the file bytes and thus the hash.
- One PDF failed because it contained a hidden OCR text layer that changed after our initial normalization pass (the OCR pipeline appended a metadata stamp).

Remediation steps I'm executing now (ETA ~4 hours):
1) Re-export the PDFs as flattened PDF/A-2b (disable OCR layer append).
2) Recompute per-file SHA256 checksums on a Linux build agent and produce a manifest with LF-only line endings (sha256_manifest.csv).
3) Generate a detached PGP signature for the manifest (signature included in upload).
4) Upload using Whistic bulk API endpoint with multipart fingerprints and a retry strategy (see link).

I'll attach the regenerated sha256_manifest.csv when ready. If Acme wants a small proof bundle first I can upload a 3-file subset for you to validate before the full ingest.

Notes for operations: use sha256sum --binary and confirm file sizes with stat -c%s to match the manifest. Do not run any additional normalization after checksum.

-Karthik
Principal Platform Engineer — Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Attachment: sha256_manifest.csv
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-18 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SIG bundle upload — missing files and checksum mismatch

Thanks Karthik — this remediation plan looks good. Tessa, for procurement records I'll need:
- The final sha256_manifest.csv and the detached PGP signature.
- A short one‑page note (bullet list) of what changed from the original bundle (line endings, OCR stamping, files re-exported).
- The Whistic ticket ID and upload logs (to attach to the Acme procurement packet).

I can prepare the compliance cover note once the artifacts are in place; please flag if you want me to notify Acme directly or if Tessa will send the re-ingest confirmation.

Marissa Cole
Compliance Program Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Elena Bates <elena.bates@acmeinc.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-18 16:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SIG bundle upload — missing files and checksum mismatch

Appreciate the quick turnaround. A 3-file proof bundle would be perfect — please include the sha256_manifest.csv and signature. If that verifies cleanly we'll approve the full ingest.

We do not need the compliance cover note before ingest but please keep it handy for the vendor packet. ETA by COB today works for Acme.

Thanks,
Elena
